concept.name: RAG Retrieval Pipelines

relationships.description: Connects RAG Retrieval Pipelines to llm prompt engineering in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Production RAG retrieval combines semantic chunking, hybrid dense (HNSW) + sparse (BM25/SPLADE) search, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), metadata pre-filtering, and cross-encoder reranking to deliver high-precision context to LLMs.
spark.keyTakeaway: Dense vector search alone misses exact SKUs and error codes; hybrid retrieval (BM25 + HNSW) fused via RRF and narrowed by a cross-encoder reranker boosts precision while cutting LLM prompt tokens.

concept.whyItMatters: An LLM can only reason over the context it receives. Naive "embed 500-char chunks + cosine top-5" pipelines fail on exact identifiers, leak cross-tenant data when ACLs are applied too late, and flood the LLM with noisy chunks that trigger hallucinations and high token bills.
whenToUse: Grounding LLM answers in private, rapidly changing enterprise docs, support runbooks, or product catalogs.
Queries mixing semantic intent ('how to fix timeout') with exact tokens ('ERR_CONNECTION_RESET', 'SKU-9040').
Multi-tenant applications requiring strict document-level RBAC/ACL enforcement before chunks ever reach the LLM.
whenNotToUse: Small, static corpora (<50k tokens) that fit cleanly inside a prompt cache with zero retrieval latency or chunking loss.
Structured analytical queries ('sum Q3 revenue by region') where Text-to-SQL or APIs beat unstructured chunk retrieval.
Real-time streaming telemetry where indexing lag makes vector stores perpetually stale.
keyPoints: Hybrid search pairs dense embeddings (e.g., BGE-M3 / text-embedding-3-large) with lexical BM25/SPLADE so neither synonyms nor exact codes are missed.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF: sum(1 / (k + rank)), k=60) merges dense and sparse rankings cleanly without score-normalization tuning.
Cross-encoder rerankers (e.g., Cohere Rerank v3, bge-reranker-v2-m3) jointly score query+chunk pairs, pruning top-50 candidates to top-5 high-precision chunks.
Metadata pre-filtering (tenant_id, ACLs, date) must execute inside the vector/lexical index—post-filtering can return zero valid results.
Parent-child (small-to-big) chunking retrieves crisp 256-token child chunks for matching, then injects their 1,024-token parent section for LLM coherence.

examples.title: Hybrid Support Copilot for Exact Hardware SKUs
examples.scenario: A dense-only Qdrant pipeline fails when engineers search for 'AX-9040-V2 firmware rollback', returning generic router docs instead of the exact SKU manual.
examples.outcome: Adding BM25 + dense HNSW fused with RRF (k=60) and a bge-reranker-v2-m3 top-50->5 stage lifts Recall@5 by 18% and cuts LLM input tokens by 70%.

examples.title: Multi-Tenant ACL Pre-Filtering Fix
examples.scenario: A SaaS RAG service fetches top-10 vector matches globally and filters out unauthorized tenant_id rows afterward.
examples.outcome: For smaller tenants, all 10 global hits belong to larger tenants, leaving 0 context chunks; moving tenant_id and ACLs into HNSW pre-filtering fixes empty responses and eliminates leakage risk.

tradeOffs.pro: Boosts NDCG@5 by ~8-15% and slashes irrelevant context sent to the LLM.
tradeOffs.con: Adds ~40-90 ms of GPU inference latency per query on top-50 candidates.

tradeOffs.pro: Small chunks (200-300 tokens) yield sharper embedding similarity without topic dilution.
tradeOffs.con: Small chunks lose surrounding headers/conditions unless paired with parent-document expansion.

tradeOffs.pro: Hybrid dense + BM25 captures both conceptual paraphrases and exact identifiers.
tradeOffs.con: Requires maintaining synchronized dense HNSW and inverted lexical indices.

failureModes.name: Post-Retrieval ACL Starvation
failureModes.description: Filtering permissions after top-K vector search drops authorized results when other tenants dominate the top K.
failureModes.mitigation: Apply tenant_id and group ACL filters as pre-filters inside Qdrant, Milvus, OpenSearch, or pgvector.

failureModes.name: Chunk Boundary Context Shredding
failureModes.description: Fixed 500-character splits cut tables, code blocks, or 'NOT recommended' caveats away from their subject.
failureModes.mitigation: Use structure-aware Markdown/HTML splitters and parent-child retrieval (match child, return parent).

failureModes.name: Stale Index & Orphaned Chunks
failureModes.description: Updating a source document appends new chunks without deleting old chunk IDs, causing contradictory answers.
failureModes.mitigation: Key chunks deterministically by (doc_id, chunk_index) and run atomic delete-by-doc_id upserts.

failureModes.name: Lost-in-the-Middle Context Overload
failureModes.description: Stuffing 20+ unranked chunks into the prompt degrades LLM attention on middle passages and raises hallucination.
failureModes.mitigation: Rerank top-50 down to top-5/8 and place highest-scoring chunks at the start and end of the context window.

commonMistakes: Relying on pure cosine similarity for domains rich in part numbers, error codes, legal citations, or acronyms.
Splitting PDFs and Markdown tables mid-row with naive fixed character windows.
Applying RBAC/tenant filters in application code after vector search instead of inside the index.
Shipping without offline retrieval metrics (Recall@K, MRR, NDCG@10) and only eyeballing 5 sample prompts.
Passing top-25 raw chunks directly to the LLM instead of reranking down to top-5.

sections.content:
## The idea

A production RAG pipeline is a multi-stage information retrieval funnel, not a single vector lookup. Dense bi-encoder embeddings excel at semantic similarity ('memory leak' <-> 'OOM killer'), but compress away exact lexical tokens ('CVE-2024-3094', '0x80070005'). Conversely, BM25 excels at exact terms but misses synonyms.

Modern pipelines solve this with **two-stage hybrid retrieval**: a fast **Stage 1 recall layer** runs dense HNSW vector search and sparse BM25/SPLADE in parallel (pre-filtered by tenant ACLs), merges them with **Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)**, and passes the top ~50 candidates to a **Stage 2 cross-encoder reranker** that jointly attends over `(query, chunk)` pairs to emit the top 5–8 highest-signal chunks.

## Concrete walkthrough

Trace a user query `"Why did checkout fail with ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_409?"`:

1. **Query prep & ACLs**: Extract `tenant_id=acme` and `role=eng` pre-filters; optionally expand abbreviations.
2. **Parallel Stage-1 recall**:
   - **Dense (HNSW, `1024-dim` BGE-M3)** returns top-50 semantically related checkout retry docs.
   - **Sparse (BM25 / OpenSearch)** returns top-50 docs containing the exact token `ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_409`.
3. **RRF fusion (`k=60`)**: Each doc gets `score = 1/(60 + rank_dense) + 1/(60 + rank_sparse)`, promoting docs strong in either or both lists.
4. **Stage-2 cross-encoder rerank**: `bge-reranker-v2-m3` scores the top-50 fused chunks in ~55 ms, selecting the top-5.
5. **Parent-child expansion**: Each matched 256-token child chunk expands to its 1,024-token parent section before entering the LLM prompt.

sections.content:
## Chunking & ingestion architecture

Retrieval quality is capped by ingestion quality:

- **Structure-first splitting**: Parse PDFs/HTML into Markdown headings, tables, and code blocks first; never split a table or code fence in half.
- **Parent-child (small-to-big)**: Index `256-token` child chunks for crisp vector matching, but store a `parent_id` pointing to the `1,024-token` section so the LLM sees complete context.
- **Contextual headers**: Prepend `doc_title > section_h2 > updated_at` to each chunk before embedding so pronoun-heavy paragraphs ('It must be rotated every 90 days') stay grounded.

## Retrieval stage latency & quality breakdown

| Stage | Typical Latency | Candidate Pool | Primary Strength | Failure Without It |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dense HNSW** | ~10–25 ms | Top 50 | Paraphrases, synonyms, conceptual intent | Misses exact error codes, SKUs, and IDs |
| **BM25 / SPLADE** | ~8–20 ms | Top 50 | Exact identifiers, acronyms, rare terms | Misses semantic phrasing mismatches |
| **RRF (`k=60`)** | <1 ms | Top 50 merged | Scale-invariant rank merging | Requires brittle min-max score tuning |
| **Cross-Encoder** | ~40–90 ms | 50 -> Top 5 | Full query-chunk token attention | Noisy top-20 floods LLM and raises cost |

## Failure modes

RAG pipelines silently degrade in four ways:

- **Post-filtering empty sets**: Applying permissions after top-K retrieval starves minority tenants.
- **Stale chunk orphans**: Re-ingesting edited docs without deleting prior chunk IDs causes old policies to outrank new ones.
- **Embedding model drift**: Mixing query embeddings from model v2 against document embeddings from model v1 silently destroys cosine similarity.
- **Table flattening**: Naive PDF text extractors scramble multi-column financial or spec tables into unreadable word soup.

## Evaluating retrieval separately from generation

Always decouple **retrieval evals** from **LLM generation evals**:

1. **Retrieval metrics**: Build a 100–300 query golden set with labeled relevant `doc_ids` and track `Recall@20` (Stage 1) and `NDCG@5` / `MRR` (Stage 2).
2. **Generation metrics**: Measure groundedness/faithfulness (does the answer contradict or extrapolate beyond retrieved chunks?) and citation accuracy using frameworks like `RAGAS` or LLM-as-a-judge.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Enforce `tenant_id` and ACL predicates as **pre-filters** inside the vector and lexical indices.
- [ ] Combine dense HNSW + BM25/SPLADE with **RRF (`k=60`)** instead of dense-only search.
- [ ] Add a **cross-encoder reranker** (`top-50 -> top-5`) to maximize precision and cut LLM input tokens.
- [ ] Use **structure-aware chunking** with contextual headers (`doc_title > section`) and atomic `delete-by-doc_id` upserts.
- [ ] Track `Recall@20` and `NDCG@5` on a golden query set before changing chunk sizes, embedders, or prompts.

nodes.label: BM25 / SPLADE Index
nodes.role: Exact SKU, error code & keyword top-50

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Production RAG retrieval combines semantic chunking, hybrid dense (HNSW) + sparse (BM25/SPLADE) search, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), metadata pre-filtering, and cross-encoder reranking to deliver high-precision context to LLMs.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: BM25 / SPLADE Index applies the primary invariant and coordinates with RRF + Cross-Encoder.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, RRF + Cross-Encoder experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Apply tenant_id and group ACL filters as pre-filters inside Qdrant, Milvus, OpenSearch, or pgvector.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Dense vector search alone misses exact SKUs and error codes; hybrid retrieval (BM25 + HNSW) fused via RRF and narrowed by a cross-encoder reranker boosts precision while cutting LLM prompt tokens.
Avoid trap: Relying on pure cosine similarity for domains rich in part numbers, error codes, legal citations, or acronyms.
Avoid trap: Splitting PDFs and Markdown tables mid-row with naive fixed character windows.
When to reach for it: Grounding LLM answers in private, rapidly changing enterprise docs, support runbooks, or product catalogs.
When to reach for it: Queries mixing semantic intent ('how to fix timeout') with exact tokens ('ERR_CONNECTION_RESET', 'SKU-9040').

putItTogether.summary: Dense vector search alone misses exact SKUs and error codes; hybrid retrieval (BM25 + HNSW) fused via RRF and narrowed by a cross-encoder reranker boosts precision while cutting LLM prompt tokens.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Rag Retrieval Pipelines before scaling.

putItTogether.outcome: Adding BM25 + dense HNSW fused with RRF (k=60) and a bge-reranker-v2-m3 top-50->5 stage lifts Recall@5 by 18% and cuts LLM input tokens by 70%.
